sections.html:
Alabaster is a city in Shelby County and a southern suburb of Birmingham. It sits about 23 miles south of downtown Birmingham and 69 miles north of Montgomery, reached by U.S. 31 and by Interstate 65 at exit 238.

ItemAlabaster
IncorporatedFebruary 23, 1953
CountyShelby (seat: Columbiana)
Area25.59 square miles
Elevation482 feet
2020 census population33,284
2025 estimate34,748
ZIP codes35007 and 35114

The 2020 count made Alabaster the 16th largest city in Alabama. It is also the largest city in Shelby County, a county of 810 square miles that held 223,024 people in 2020.

sections.h2: How did Alabaster get its name and its start?
sections.html:
The name comes from the high-calcium limestone under the town. George L. Scott Sr. ran the Alabaster Lime Company, which mined it, and his shipping point was called Scott Rock.

A first try at incorporation in 1952 failed. A second petition succeeded on February 23, 1953, by a vote of 79 to 23, with 427 people living in the new town. The First Bank of Alabaster opened in 1952 under George L. Scott Jr., who later became the first mayor. In 1971 the city merged with the neighboring community of Siluria, which had incorporated in 1954.

Growth since then has been steep. The census counted 1,623 residents in 1960, 7,079 in 1980, 22,619 in 2000 and 33,284 in 2020.

sections.h2: What is the land and climate like in Alabaster?
sections.html:
Alabaster lies mostly in the Cahaba and Opossum valleys, divided by Pine Ridge, which runs north to south. Parallel ridges at the tail end of the Appalachian foothills flank both valleys.

Small creeks, including Buck Creek and Beaverdam Creek, drain the valleys toward the Cahaba River. The climate is humid subtropical, which means hot summers and mild winters.

  • Creek-side lots deserve a flood check before you list.
  • Ridge and valley terrain means lots vary a lot in slope and drainage.
  • Humid summers put air conditioning, roofs and attic ventilation on a buyer's inspection list.

Alabaster City Schools separated from the Shelby County school system on July 1, 2013, and now runs the public schools inside the city. The system includes two elementary schools, one intermediate school, one middle school and one high school.

The Wikipedia list names Creek View Elementary, Meadow View Elementary, Thompson Intermediate, Thompson Middle and Thompson High. Private options include Evangel Christian School. Shelby County Schools serves areas outside Alabaster, Hoover and Pelham.

A school zone often decides where a family buys, so a seller should know which attendance zone a house belongs to and say so up front.

sections.h2: How do roads, transit and development shape Alabaster?
sections.html:
U.S. 31 runs through the city and Interstate 65 forms the main highway link. ClasTran runs a dial-a-ride service on weekdays inside Alabaster.

The city has talked about expanding what it calls the Main Street Medical Mile along Highway 31, with more medical facilities, a future civic center and retail. In 2017 a 350,000 square foot retail complex called District 31 was announced for the corner of U.S. 31 and I-65. Wikipedia says that as of 2026 the complex remained under construction.

Large projects near a house can cut both ways for a seller: more traffic and noise for some blocks, more shops and services for others.

sections.h2: What did the 2020 census say about Alabaster households?
sections.html:
Alabaster had 11,571 households in 2020, in 11,990 housing units, and only 3.5% of units were vacant. About 40.5% of households had children under 18, and 60.5% were married-couple households.

The homeowner vacancy rate of 0.8% is very low, and only 3.5% of all units sat vacant. Those numbers describe the housing stock in 2020 and say nothing about what any one house is worth today.

sections.h2: What does Shelby County add to the Alabaster picture?
sections.html:
Shelby County is the county that holds the records for an Alabaster house, and it is a fast-growing one. The population went from 195,085 in 2010 to 223,024 in 2020, and the Census Bureau estimate for 2025 is 238,552.

  • County seat: Columbiana, where the current limestone courthouse was built from 1905 to 1906.
  • Housing: 89,060 units in 2020, 5.4% of them vacant, and 78.1% of occupied homes owner-occupied.
  • Other cities in the county: Pelham, Helena, Chelsea, Calera and Hoover, along with Montevallo and Vestavia Hills.
  • Nearby airport: Shelby County Airport handles general aviation, and Birmingham-Shuttlesworth International sits in neighboring Jefferson County.

Alabaster also appears in the Census Bureau's Alabaster-Helena census division, which grew from 33,674 residents in 1980 to 118,831 in 2010. The division covers parts of Alabaster, Helena, Pelham, Calera, Chelsea and several other places, so it reflects growth across the whole corridor.

sections.h2: What permits and building rules apply in Alabaster?
sections.html:
Permits go through the city's Building and Engineering Services department at 1953 Municipal Way, Suite 102, and you can call (205) 664-6823. The city runs its permitting through an online system called LAMA, with accounts set up at alabaster.onlama.com.

  • The city adopted the 2021 International Building Code.
  • Planning and Zoning and Engineering review projects before permits are issued, for both residential and commercial work.
  • A Code Enforcement division checks compliance with the city's ordinances.
  • The department publishes a Homeowner Guide, an Obtaining Permits guide, a permit handbook and a fee schedule.

If you replaced a roof, finished a basement or added a deck, find out whether permits were pulled. Ask the department about any open permit before you sell, because a buyer or lender may ask. Official page: Alabaster Building and Engineering Services.

sections.h2: When are property taxes due on an Alabaster house?
sections.html:
Alabama property taxes are due October 1 and delinquent after December 31, and Alabaster is in Shelby County, so the county handles assessment and collection. The state schedule sends unpaid taxes to probate court in February and advertises them in April, with a tax sale in May.

Alabama also offers a homestead exemption for owner-occupied homes of up to 160 acres. Owners under 65 may exempt up to $4,000 of assessed value from the state portion and $2,000 from the county portion, and seniors or disabled owners can qualify for much more. Owners apply at the county office, and the next buyer must apply on their own after a sale.

Recording the deed carries a state tax of 50 cents per $500 of value. On a $300,000 sale, that comes to $300. The Shelby County probate office records the deed and collects the tax.

sections.h2: What do Alabaster sellers usually face?
sections.html:
Alabaster grew from 30,352 residents in 2010 to 33,284 in 2020. A house with old systems, deferred repairs or a tenant may still call for a different path than a standard listing.

  • Inherited houses that heirs do not want to maintain.
  • Rentals with tenants in place.
  • Houses needing roofs, HVAC or foundation work.
  • Owners relocating who cannot manage a long listing.

Cash Home Buyers reviews Alabaster houses as they stand and responds with a written offer. If you decline, you owe nothing.

faqs.q: What county is Alabaster, AL in?
faqs.a: Alabaster is in Shelby County, Alabama. It is the county's largest city, while the county seat is Columbiana.

faqs.q: What is the population of Alabaster, AL?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 33,284 people, and the 2025 Census Bureau estimate is 34,748.

faqs.q: Does Alabaster have its own school system?
faqs.a: Yes. Alabaster City Schools separated from Shelby County Schools on July 1, 2013, and it operates the public schools in the city.

faqs.q: Where do I get a building permit in Alabaster?
faqs.a: From Building and Engineering Services at 1953 Municipal Way, Suite 102, or through the city's online LAMA portal. The office phone is (205) 664-6823.
